title: Who’s Trading Now?
hook: Before you read the chart, read you.

launchpad.outcome: Check your own state before a session, and catch who is making the decision in the moment.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Who is trading right now: the trader, or the feeling?

slides.headline: Before you read the chart, read yourself first.
slides.line: You’re the same person on the same morning, but a different trader can show up from minute to minute.

slides.headline: A valid setup appears, and your stomach drops.

cards.label: The trader
cards.sub: You notice the feeling, check your rule, and take it.

check.prompt: Who should be making this decision right now?

options.label: Skip it, I can’t lose again today
options.feedback: That decision wasn’t about this chart. Yesterday’s loss made that call for you.

options.label: Notice the feeling, check, then take it
options.feedback: Yes. The feeling came along for the ride, but the trader made the decision.

slides.headline: Your plan says you’re done, but you feel unstoppable.

cards.label: The trader
cards.sub: You’re done, so you journal and close.

check.prompt: Who’s doing the trading right now?

options.label: One more trade, I’m on fire
options.feedback: That’s the heater talking, not your plan. Your plan already said you were done.

options.label: I’m done, so I journal and close
options.feedback: That’s the trader. The plan said you were done, so you listened.

slides.line: 1R is the amount you planned to risk on one trade. You’re up +2R, twice that, and your plan says stop for the day.

slides.headline: Before every trade, ask yourself, “Who’s trading right now?”
slides.line: These versions of you all show up in one morning, not one at a time.

steps.label: 9:58 · after loss
steps.sub: Yesterday’s loss wants you to skip a valid setup.

steps.label: 10:20 · +2R
steps.sub: The heater wants you to take one more trade.

steps.label: 10:41 · red candle
steps.sub: Fear wants you to grab a small +15 profit and close early.

steps.label: The skill
steps.sub: You notice which version of you just took the mouse.

slides.title: Read you first
slides.body: Where would you put each thought? This is for noticing, not grading yourself.
slides.punch: A red state doesn’t make the setup invalid. It makes your personal rules matter more. (That’s Section 2.)

slides.title: Write the state down, not just the trade

example.plannedResponse: Pause and require the full checklist

slides.punch: Private to you. Never shared, never ranked.

slides.quote: I check my chart before every session. I check myself first.

slides.prompt: Which version of you shows up most, and when does she show up?
slides.modelAnswer: I notice which feeling shows up and when: after a loss, after a win, when I’m bored, when money is tight. Before every trade I ask who is trading right now.

takeaways: Before every trade: who’s trading now?
remember: BEFORE EVERY TRADE: WHO’S TRADING NOW?
